title: Randomized evaluation of Google AI flood alerts with community dissemination in Bihar, India (2022–2023 monsoons)
summary: Bihar RCT, 319 panchayats: households relayed Google flood alerts reported 16.6% fewer illness symptoms and about 30% lower medical costs.
account: Google's AI flood-forecasting system, run with India's Central Water Commission (CWC), issues riverine flood alerts as Android push notifications. In Bihar, India, economists Maulik Jagnani (Tufts) and Rohini Pande (Yale) ran a randomized evaluation across 319 panchayats in 12 flood-prone districts. It covered the 2022 and 2023 monsoon seasons (June to October). The non-governmental organization Yuganter trained community volunteers to relay the alerts. Treatment households got 2.41 more alerts in 2022 and were 46.5% more likely to get an alert before water reached their area. They reported 16.56% fewer illness symptoms and about 30% lower medical spending than controls. No specific evacuation tied to an alert is documented.
purpose: The forecasting system was built to warn people of riverine floods before water arrives so they can prepare or evacuate. The measured preparedness and health effects are that intended benefit, but only at cohort level.
system: Google flood forecasting with Android push alerts (Google Public Alerts), plus community dissemination by Yuganter volunteers
deployer: Central Water Commission of India with Google; last-mile dissemination by Yuganter (NGO) under the Jagnani-Pande evaluation
domain: Disaster risk reduction / flood early warning
segment: Rural households in riverine flood zones

ratings.reason: Effects are cohort averages across roughly 3.6 million people's communities (fewer illness symptoms, lower medical spending). No identifiable household with an attributable changed outcome is documented.
The study estimates population-level preparedness and health effects from a randomized design. It reports no discrete event such as a named evacuation.

ai_role.statement: The AI forecast generated the alerts. The randomized contrast, however, is between community dissemination of those alerts and alerts alone. So the measured effect is attributable to the dissemination of AI forecasts rather than to forecast accuracy itself. A 2019 pilot in which the only added treatment was raising alert awareness with a single local leader found no treatment impact.

produced_by: Google/CWC flood alerts available to all 319 study panchayats (both arms); the randomized element was volunteer dissemination
Trained community volunteers relaying smartphone alerts in villages with low literacy and limited location-services use
Repeated flood seasons (2022 was more intense than 2023) allowing effects to be measured
must_hold: Alerts reach households before water arrives (46.5% more likely in treatment communities in 2022)
Households trust alerts despite more false positives (8.09% vs 3.64%)
Dissemination capacity is maintained. From 2023 two volunteers per panchayat replaced three, supplemented by direct WhatsApp/SMS messages to treatment households enrolled in the 2022 endline survey.

headline: Google flood alerts in Bihar cut reported illness by 16.6%
metric: 16.56% fewer illness symptoms and about 30% lower medical expenditure

comparator.against: control communities, where households had access to the smartphone alerts but no community volunteers relaying them
comparator.after: 0.36 fewer illness symptoms (a 16.56% decrease); roughly INR 6,500 less on illness treatment (a 32.87% decrease)
comparator.quote: Overall, treatment households observed 0.36 fewer illness symptoms (a 16.56% decrease) compared to control households (Table 4). As a result, households in treatment areas incurred roughly INR 6,500 less on illness treatment (a 32.87% decrease).

later.note: Neither cited source reports a development after the 2022-2023 evaluation seasons.

value.what: less spent on illness treatment per household over the flood season
value.who: treatment households in the Bihar study panchayats
value.quote: As a result, households in treatment areas incurred roughly INR 6,500 less on illness treatment (a 32.87% decrease). In fact, based on the estimated reduction in medical expenditures alone, we estimate that for every $1 spent on the program, the intervention would generate a minimum benefit of $30 during a severe flooding season.
